eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from sources including the Met Office and BBC points to a daytime high near 27°C in Wuhan on June 13 under mostly cloudy skies with light southerly winds and a chance of showers. Trader emphasis on 25–26°C reflects uncertainty over cloud thickness and precipitation timing, which can sharply reduce solar insolation and enhance evaporative cooling. Key differentiating factors include the extent of low-level moisture and convective development typical of early East Asian monsoon transitions, versus clearer breaks that would allow temperatures to reach or exceed 27°C. Historical June variability, with early-month highs often 2–4°C below mid-month averages around 30–31°C, further supports the close 25–26°C clustering in current odds. Updated short-range guidance expected within the next 12–24 hours could refine these thresholds before resolution.

Current model consensus from sources such as the BBC and timeanddate shows a high of approximately 15 °C (59 °F) under post-frontal conditions, with north-westerly winds, scattered showers, and limited sunshine keeping temperatures suppressed. A cold front that made landfall over the Western Cape around June 11–12 has introduced cooler, moister air, shifting the expected peak 2–3 °C below the June mean.  

This alignment of recent frontal passage, stable post-frontal steering, and model agreement explains why the market-implied probabilities concentrate on 15 °C (40.5 %), 16 °C (26 %), and 14 °C (19.5 %), while outcomes above 17 °C or below 13 °C remain low-probability outliers.
